RFC9494-3.1-1.note: Forbidden: declaring code 71 without code 64. TestRFC9494_LLGRCapDeclaredWithGRCap fails unless extractGRCapabilities returns one code-64 declaration for the same peer as the code-71 one (require.Len grCaps 1, Code 64, same Peers). Negative: TestRFC9494_NoLLGRCapWithoutGRContainer places long-lived-stale-time outside the graceful-restart container and fails if either code 71 or code 64 is declared, so no config shape yields 71 alone.

RFC9494-3.1-2.note: Two clauses, both asserted. Sender: TestRFC9494_FlagsReservedBitsZeroOnSend fails unless the encoded Flags octet is exactly 0x80 (any reserved bit set goes red). Receiver: TestRFC9494_FlagsReservedBitsIgnoredOnReceive fails if a 0xFF Flags octet errors or decodes differently from 0x80, and if 0x7F leaks into the F bit.

RFC9494-4-1.note: RFC 9494 Section 4: "If a BGP speaker is configured to support the procedures of this document, it MUST use BGP Capabilities Advertisement [RFC5492] to advertise the Long-Lived Graceful Restart Capability." Re-judged 2026-10-15 after the positive tag's claim was reworded (body unchanged): extractLLGRCapabilities is declared through grCapabilities, the plugin's BGPCapabilityExtractor (gr_capability.go), which the claim now names. TestExtractLLGRCapabilities_Basic fails unless extractLLGRCapabilities emits one Code 71 hex declaration for the peer whose payload decodes to LLST 3600. Negative: TestExtractLLGRCapabilities_NoLLGR asserts no declaration without long-lived-stale-time. Proven at the plugin's capability-declaration boundary; the hand-off to the OPEN is not asserted in these units.

RFC9494-4.1-1.note: Forbidden: honouring code 71 received without code 64. TestHandleStructuredOpenLLGRNoGR sends an OPEN with only code 71 and fails if peerLLGRCaps holds the peer (assert.False llgrOK), which is the map onSessionDown reads. Negative: TestHandleStructuredOpenGRPlusLLGR keeps both capabilities when code 64 is present, with families, F bits and LLST 7200/3600 asserted.

RFC9494-4.2-1.note: RFC 9494 Section 4.2: 'After the session goes down, and before the session is re-established, the stale routes for an AFI/SAFI MUST be retained.' Read in its bounded GR-plus-LLST, zero-period and omitted-family context. Re-read all ten tagged units: gr_state_test.go TestLLSTTimerExpiry_LastFamily and TestOnTimerExpired_WithoutLLGR; rfc9494_llgr_entry_test.go TestRFC9494ZeroRestartTimeRetainsThroughTheLLGRPeriod, TestRFC9494BothTimesZeroRetainsNothing, TestRFC9494RestartTimeThenLongLivedStaleTime and TestRFC9494DelayedDownPreservesLLSTDeadlines; rfc9494_omitted_gr_family_test.go TestLLGROmittedGRFamilyRetainsRealRIB, TestLLGROmittedGRFamilyTimerSurvivesConventionalEntry, TestLLGROmittedGRFamilyWithoutLLSTIsRemoved and TestLLGROmittedGRFamilyReadvertisementDoesNotDelaySiblingExpiry, all under internal/component/bgp/plugins/gr/. The legacy callback-only units are not sufficient alone. The real registered-RIB units assert received-route existence before DOWN, retention at GR level 1 and LLGR level 2, both-zero deletion, and distinct before/at absolute deadlines on JSON and structured paths. Empty/mixed GR lists retain omitted exchanged LLGR families immediately; zero or unexchanged omitted families disappear. Virtual-time checks require presence one nanosecond before expiry and absence at expiry, preserve sibling retention, and prevent delayed DOWN dispatch or blocked readvertisement from extending the bound. This closes the earlier family-omission and timing evidence gaps rather than relying on timer-map presence. Producing symbols: gr.go::handleStateEvent, handleStructuredState, retainPeerFamilies, wireStateCallbacks; gr_state.go::onSessionDownDeferred, startRestartTimer, handleTimerExpired, enterLLGRLocked, handleLLSTExpired. Native panic records establish producer reachability only; semantic discrimination comes from those exact inventory/state/deadline assertions. This verdict covers this row's pre-reestablishment retention obligation, not separately recorded consecutive-restart, resynchronization or egress-community findings. No new check or interop run is claimed.

RFC9494-4.2-2.note: RFC 9494 Section 4.2: 'For each AFI/SAFI for which it has received a nonzero Long-Lived Stale Time, the helper router MUST start a timer for that Long-Lived Stale Time.' Its chapeau requires LLGR entry after the family's Restart Time, including zero. Re-read all eight tagged units: gr_state_test.go TestOnTimerExpired_WithLLGR and TestOnSessionDown_ZeroGR_ZeroLLST; rfc9494_llgr_entry_test.go TestRFC9494RestartTimeThenLongLivedStaleTime and TestRFC9494BothTimesZeroRetainsNothing; all four TestLLGROmittedGRFamily tests in rfc9494_omitted_gr_family_test.go, under internal/component/bgp/plugins/gr/. Callback occurrence and eventual deletion alone remain weak evidence, but the added real-RIB virtual-time tests pin received durations: omitted IPv4 LLST 2 expires at DOWN+2 while IPv6 GR 6 transitions at DOWN+6 and LLST 4 expires at DOWN+10; the omitted LLST 8 case survives sibling GR entry and expires at DOWN+8 rather than restarting. Each principal boundary asserts presence immediately before and absence at the boundary. A blocked immediate-family readvertisement still permits sibling GR 1 then LLST 2 to expire at DOWN+3. Both production event paths are exercised. Zero/unexchanged omitted families explicitly have no timer and no retained route; both-zero state is inactive. These assertions distinguish wrong timer duration, delayed start, shared-family deadlines, missing timer and timer replacement. Producing symbols: gr.go::handleStateEvent, handleStructuredState, retainPeerFamilies, wireStateCallbacks; gr_state.go::onSessionDownDeferred, startRestartTimer, handleTimerExpired, enterLLGRLocked, handleLLSTExpired. Native producer-panic records prove reachability, not duration correctness. No new check or interop run is claimed, and neighboring restart/resynchronization findings remain unchanged.

RFC9494-4.2-3.note: Independently reread RFC9494 Section 4.2: 'If the timer for the Long-Lived Stale Time for a given AFI/SAFI expires before the session is re-established, the helper MUST delete all stale routes of that AFI/SAFI from the neighbor that it is retaining.' Preserve the settled pre-reestablishment judgment after rereading all three tagged functions and their actual registered RIB consumer. TestLLSTTimerExpiry_SingleFamily observes the expired IPv4 family with IPv6 still retained; TestRFC9494LLSTExpiryDeletesTheFamilysStaleRoutes exercises production wireStateCallbacks and requires the specific IPv4 purge command while forbidding the unexpired IPv6 purge. TestRFC9494DelayedDownPreservesLLSTDeadlines supplies the decisive actual-storage assertions on JSON and structured DOWN: both-live, one-expired, both-expired and zero-GR cases; one retained level-2 route with literal LLGR_STALE and active retention before each original deadline, including one nanosecond before; actual absence and cleared family retention at expiry; peer release at the last deadline. newGRWithRealRIB invokes the registered bgp-rib engine and real execute-command RPC, not a deletion mock. The current callback routes to the explicitly registered purgeStaleCommand. Its replacement deletion boundary selects StaleLevel>Fresh and removes entries under PeerRIB's storage lock, the same lock as inserts, collecting only successfully removed native identity, received ADD-PATH presence/value and message generation. Sent cleanup selects those removed owners, not old projections merely absent from a newer received table, captures the sent receipt, dispatches after unlocking, and reaches the command/batch/final expected-owner consumer. The final writer rejects obsolete receipts. This preserves the clause while avoiding withdrawal of a newer received owner. The four physical80 runs and omitted/reset controls remain retained evidence, not substitutes for this clause mapping and not proof of synchronization, consecutive-restart, other LLGR gaps, or universal destination-FIB behavior. Native handleTimerExpired halts bind reachability only.

RFC9494-4.2-4.note: RFC 9494 §4.2: "The helper router MUST attach the LLGR_STALE community to the stale routes being retained." Read all three tagged carriers: internal/component/bgp/plugins/gr/rfc9494_llgr_entry_test.go::TestRFC9494ZeroRestartTimeRetainsThroughTheLLGRPeriod exercises production wireStateCallbacks on JSON and structured DOWN, real registered RIB commands, and requires retained received route 198.51.100.0/24 at level 2 with community 0xffff0006. internal/component/bgp/plugins/rib/rfc9494_rib_gr_test.go::TestAttachCommunity checks the actual stored bundle contains that exact value; internal/component/bgp/plugins/rib/rfc9494_test.go::TestRFC9494_FreshRoutesDoNotGetLLGRStale requires zero attachments, unchanged fresh level and no community for a fresh route. Two positive and one negative tags. gr.go::wireStateCallbacks dispatches deletion of NO_LLGR before attach-community, then raises stale level and triggers per-family readvertisement; rib_commands_community.go::attachCommunityCommand filters fresh entries and attachCommunity updates the bundle and clears the original-wire fingerprint. Removing marker attachment or attaching it to fresh routes breaks different assertions. The RFC note "Note that this requirement implies that the routes would need to be readvertised in order to disseminate the modified community" is traced to wireStateCallbacks::onLLGREntryDone; tagged units establish the attachment obligation at storage, not a destination-wire guarantee. Supplementary untagged test/plugin/llgr-peer-stale-time-drives-timer.ci waits for a destination LLGR_STALE UPDATE before acknowledging the phase. This verdict does not erase RFC9494-4.3-2 further-advertisement protection gap or claim every LLGR activation case is implemented (see 4.2-1/-2). No runtime renewal performed. Post-lint independent source rejudgment: the changed zero-Restart-Time tagged unit still compares the retained route community to literal 0xffff0006 on both event rails after real RIB DOWN; removing testPeer helper arguments leaves bytes and peer identity identical. Re-read TestAttachCommunity and the fresh-route negative as well as wireStateCallbacks: delete NO_LLGR, attach LLGR_STALE, raise level, then readvertise. The distinct fresh-route input must remain unmarked. Enforced attachment judgment is unchanged; cleanup now reports mux.Close failures. Destination-wire dissemination and missing-GR-family activation are not newly proven by this lint repair.

RFC9494-4.2-5.note: Independently rejudged 2026-10-22 against test/draft/plugin/llgr-import-no-llgr.ci, not its still-old-syntax live counterpart; pending until parent promotion and stamping. No execution. RFC 9494 Section 4.2: "If any of the routes from the peer have been marked with the NO_LLGR community, either as sent by the peer or as the result of a configured policy, they MUST NOT be retained and MUST be removed as per the normal operation of [RFC4271]." Read every carrier: internal/component/bgp/plugins/gr/rfc9494_llgr_entry_test.go::TestRFC9494ZeroRestartTimeRetainsThroughTheLLGRPeriod; rib/rfc9494_rib_gr_test.go::TestDeleteWithCommunity; rib/rfc9494_test.go::TestRFC9494_StaleRouteWithoutNoLLGRRetained; rib/rfc9494_no_llgr_withdraw_test.go::TestRFC9494NoLLGRSweepWithdrawsTheBestPath and TestRFC9494SweepKeepsTheBestPathWithoutNoLLGR; both polarities of the named draft and internal/test/fixture/plugin_fixture_llgr_import.go::llgrImportNoLLGR. The GR carrier drives both JSON and structured DOWN paths with real received routes and requires the NO_LLGR route absent while the sibling survives at stale level 2 with LLGR_STALE. Exact community deletion and retention controls distinguish ffff0007 from LLGR_STALE and the real nonmatching 65001:100 community. The best-change pair requires exactly one IPv4/unicast Withdraw for 10.0.0.0/24 versus unchanged storage and no event. In the pending CI, both source UPDATEs lack communities; only marked has import { filters [ modify:NO-LLGR ]; final accept; }. The observer requires NO_LLGR on 10.0.0.0/24 and its absence from the plain control before sending TCP marker announcements that release both close actions; afterwards it requires marked absence and plain retention with LLGR_STALE before the stderr success fence. The explicit final preserves the modifier and the original assertions rather than bypassing policy. Producer/consumer chain read: filter_modify/config.go::parseCommOps and modify.go::buildDynamicDelta produce community-add; gr/gr.go::wireStateCallbacks issues delete-with-community before adding LLGR_STALE; rib/rib_commands_community.go::registerCommunityCommands explicitly routes that command to deleteWithCommunityCommand, which selectively removes stale matching routes, dispatches sent lifecycle reconciliation and recomputes/publishes best changes. Both peer-added and policy-added clauses remain evidenced compositionally. Preserve the existing scope: the import CI observes received RIB, not downstream recipient TCP, and no destination-wire proof or fresh functional green is claimed. Parent owns native freshness, draft promotion and the stamp.

RFC9494-4.2-6.note: The row obliges every Section 4.3 procedure. The tagged units prove one: TestRFC9494_LLGRStaleRouteIsLeastPreferred fails unless attach-community raises StaleLevel to the depreference threshold and the stale LOCAL_PREF 500 candidate loses to a fresh LOCAL_PREF 100; the negative keeps an unmarked route competing normally. The other Section 4.3 procedures (LLGR_STALE on receipt from the peer, NO_LLGR handling, advertisement restrictions) have no assertion in these units.

RFC9494-4.2-8.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after 0b323594c4). RFC 9494 Section 4.2: "once the LLGR Period begins, the Helper MUST immediately remove all the stale routes from the peer that it is retaining for that address family if any of the following occur", with three bullets. All three now carry exact assertions on onSessionReestablished: F bit clear in the new LLGR capability while the new GR capability sets it (TestOnSessionReestablished_LLGRFBitClearPurges, purged == [ipv4/unicast], peer released), family omitted from the new LLGR capability with a listed sibling kept (TestOnSessionReestablished_FamilyAbsentFromLLGRPurges, purged == exactly ipv4/unicast, ipv6/unicast still retained), GR present with no LLGR capability (TestOnSessionReestablished_NoLLGRCapPurgesLLGRPeriodFamily), and neither capability (TestOnSessionReestablished_DuringLLGR_NoCaps). Each fixture sets the GR F bit, so the RFC 4724 rule cannot produce the purge and only the LLGR branch of reconnectKeepsFamily can: the former GR-seeded union would leave all three new positives empty. Negatives are conforming controls, not neighbouring errors: both F bits set keeps the family until EOR (TestOnSessionReestablished_BothFBitsSetKeepsLLGRPeriodFamily, TestOnSessionReestablished_DuringLLGR), and a family still in its GR period is not judged by the LLGR bullets (TestOnSessionReestablished_GRPeriodFamilyIgnoresLLGRBullets), matching "once the LLGR Period begins" per family. A purge-every-LLGR-family fix turns those red. Residual seams: the tagged units decide at the state manager; the purge-stale dispatch over the returned families in gr.go handleStateEvent is the loop RFC4724-4.2-8 dispatch tests drive, and no .ci runs an LLGR reconnect with per-family LLGR F bits (llgr-reconnect-fbit-purge.ci needs a ze-peer option). 2026-10-18 (owner-approved claim edit): the DuringLLGR and DuringLLGR_NoCaps tag claims no longer cite line numbers or the removed newForwarding map, and now state only what their bodies assert (both F bits set: no family purged; neither capability: the one LLGR-period family purged and the peer no longer active). Assertions unchanged; fresh revert discrimination records on onSessionReestablished.

RFC9494-4.3-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent reviewer, over the uncommitted rfc9494_llgr_self_attach_test.go). RFC 9494 Section 4.3: "A BGP speaker that has advertised the Long-Lived Graceful Restart Capability to a neighbor MUST perform the following upon receiving a route from that neighbor with the LLGR_STALE community or upon attaching the LLGR_STALE community itself per Section 4.2: * Treat the route as the least preferred in route selection". The previous verdict was weak only for the second trigger, "upon attaching the LLGR_STALE community itself". It is closed: TestRFC9494SelfAttachedLLGRStaleIsLeastPreferred drives the RIB's own mark-stale then attach-community ffff0006 commands (the pair onLLGREnter dispatches, gr.go) and asserts SelectBestExplain over the gathered candidates is decided at BestStepStale for the fresh LOCAL_PREF 100 route against the retained LOCAL_PREF 200 route whose peer address is also lower, so every ordinary step favours the loser and only the depreference can decide. Go-overlay mutants, observed: deleting `entry.StaleLevel = storage.DepreferenceThreshold` in attachCommunityCommand turns the positive red (decided at a later step, 192.0.2.1 wins), which also shows mark-stale alone stays below the threshold; disabling the StaleLevelFresh guard in the attach sweep turns only the negative red (the route stored fresh after mark-stale is depreferenced and loses). Both tests passed -count=5. The received-route trigger stands as judged before: negotiateWith -> LLGRIngressFilter -> RIB Step 0 and llgr-stale-received-depreferenced.ci over the daemon. Residual, not a weakness of the assertions: onLLGREnter also dispatches mark-stale level 2 after the attach (gr.go), a second producer of the same depreference, so the production sequence stays compliant if either one alone is removed; the self-attach unit pins the attach producer the sentence names, and no unit tagged for this row drives onLLGREnter into the RIB's selection. The two new discrimination records are body-panic reverts and show reachability only; the semantic mutants above are the discriminating evidence.

RFC9494-4.3-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent reviewer, over the uncommitted rfc9494_llgr_cached_forward_test.go). RFC 9494 Section 4.3: "The route SHOULD NOT be advertised to any neighbor from which the Long-Lived Graceful Restart Capability has not been received. The exception is described in Section 4.6. Note that this requirement implies that such routes should be withdrawn from any such neighbor." The previous verdict's gap, the live cache-forward rail, is closed on both rails: an LLGR_STALE UPDATE received through notifyMessageReceiver and forwarded from the recent-update cache must hand the egress step stale uint8(2) and leave the destination only the withdrawal, and the same UPDATE from a session that did not advertise LLGR must reach it as an announcement. Go-overlay mutants, observed: dropping `Meta: routeMeta` from the cached ReceivedUpdate reddens both advertised subtests; passing nil meta in forwardUpdateSection's egress call reddens only the cached-forward test; passing nil in reactorForwardRSSection's reddens only the route-server test; forcing llgrAdvertised true in notifyMessageReceiver reddens both not-advertised subtests. The reviewer changed the stand-in egress step to request withdrawal through mods.SetWithdraw and accept, which is what LLGREgressFilter does, instead of refusing, so the rails' withdraw conversion is the path asserted; both rails still emit the withdrawal. The other links stand as judged before: LLGREgressFilter withdraws for a non-LLGR EBGP neighbor and passes level 1, the relay, peer-up, resend and refresh rails carry the source ingress level. The stale marking of a received route is LLGRIngressFilter's, proven under RFC9494-4.3-1's tags; this row is judged on its own text, given a route already marked. Residual, not a weakness of the assertions: no daemon test shows the EBGP withdrawal on the wire, and the discrimination records are body-panic reverts, whose negative records go red at the positive subtest before the negative one runs.

RFC9494-4.4-1.note: Forbidden: a least-preferred route beating one that is not. TestSelectBest_LLGRStaleDepreference gives the stale candidate LOCAL_PREF 300 against 100 and fails, in both input orders, unless the normal route wins, so removing Step 0 goes red. Negative: TestSelectBest_BothLLGRStale fails unless two stale candidates fall through to LOCAL_PREF, so the rule orders only across the least-preferred boundary.

The shared fixture rfc9494Opens now lists IPv4 AND IPv6 unicast in both GR Capabilities (TLV and JSON 00000001018000020180), so IPv6 reaches the LLGR decision. Negative TestRFC9494HelperProceduresOffWithoutLocalConfig (no code 71, or IPv6 only): no ffff0007/ffff0006 for ipv4. Positive TestRFC9494HelperProceduresOnPerConfiguredFamily (Ze declares IPv4, peer IPv4+IPv6): both LLGR commands for ipv4/unicast, exactly neither delete-with-community ffff0007 nor attach-community ffff0006 for ipv6/unicast, and purge-stale ipv6/unicast.
